content: The following information provides a detailed overview of the use of tocolytic agents, their dosages, and associated outcomes in the management of preterm labor, as well as maternal and neonatal outcomes: 1. Calcium Channel Blockers: Nifedipine was studied in various dosages and routes of administration: 20 mg orally (3 trial arms). 20 mg orally combined with 10 mg sublingually (1 trial arm). 10 or 20 mg orally (1 trial arm). 5 mg sublingually (1 trial arm). 10 mg orally (5 trial arms). 10 mg, route unspecified (1 trial arm). 10 mg sublingually (8 trial arms). 20 mg orally combined with 10 mg sublingually (1 trial arm). 20 mg orally (8 trial arms). 30 mg orally (10 trial arms). 30 mg sublingually (1 trial arm). 10–40 mg sublingually (1 trial arm). Nicardipine was evaluated in the following dosages: 2 mg/min intravenously (1 trial arm). 3 mg/hour intravenously (1 trial arm). 40 mg orally (1 trial arm). 2. Magnesium Sulfate: Administered in the following dosages: 4 g intravenously (3 trial arms). 6 g intravenously (1 trial arm). 75 mg intravenously (11 trial arms). 300 µg/min intravenously (1 trial arm). 3. Nitric Oxide Donors: Glyceryl trinitrate was used transdermally in 2 trial arms. Isosorbide dinitrate was administered sublingually in 1 trial arm. 4. Maternal Outcomes: Serious adverse effects were reported with varying frequencies across different tocolytic agents, ranging from 15% to 90%, though many outcomes were not estimable. Treatment cessation due to side effects was observed in up to 92% of cases with some agents, with varying levels of certainty regarding the increase in side effects. Specific side effects included: Palpitations: Likely increased in 65% of cases. Headache: Possibly increased in 72% of cases. Nausea or vomiting: Likely increased in 72% of cases. Tachycardia: Possibly increased in 34% of cases. Cardiac arrhythmias: Rare, with an estimated rate of 6 per 1000 cases. Hypotension: No significant difference in 62% of cases. Pulmonary edema: Absolute effects were not estimable in most cases. Dyspnea: Likely increased in 78% of cases. Maternal infection: Uncertain outcomes in 70% of cases. 5. Fetal and Neonatal Outcomes: Perinatal death: No significant difference in 51% of cases. Fetal death: No significant difference in 46% of cases. Neonatal death before 28 days: No significant difference in 66 per 1000 cases. Respiratory morbidity: Likely no difference in 39% of cases. Neurodevelopmental morbidity: Possibly reduced in 42% of cases. Gastrointestinal morbidity: Uncertain in 37% of cases. Neonatal infection: No significant difference in 37% of cases. Mean birth weight: Likely no difference in 13% of cases. Birth weight <2000 g: No significant difference in 25% of cases. Birth weight <2500 g: Likely reduced in 6% of cases. 6. References: The data is supported by numerous studies and systematic reviews, including those published in reputable journals such as The Lancet, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology. These studies provide insights into the efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness of tocolytic agents in delaying preterm birth and improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. This comprehensive analysis highlights the variability in outcomes associated with different tocolytic agents and underscores the importance of individualized treatment approaches based on clinical circumstances and patient needs.
